text: Source & Credits What is Sickle Cell Disease? x SCD is a group of inherited red blood cell disorders. x Healthy red blood cells are round, & they move through small blood vessels to carry oxygen to all parts of the body. x In someone who has SCD, the red blood cells become hard & sticky & look like a C-shaped farm tool called a “sickle”. PMF IAS – Learn Smart 145 x The sickle cells die early, which causes a constant shortage of red blood cells. x Also, when they travel through small blood vessels, they get stuck & clog the blood flow. This can cause pain & other serious problems such infection, acute chest syndrome & stroke. Source & Credits Tuberculosis (TB) x Tuberculosis (TB) is an infectious disease caused by Mycobacterium tuberculosis. x TB commonly affects the lungs (pulmonary TB) but can also affect other parts (extra pulmonary TB). x It spreads from person to person through the air, when people who are infected with TB infection cough, sneeze or otherwise transmit respiratory fluids through the air. x The most common risk factor associated with TB is HIV and other conditions that impair the immune system. x Symptomatic Diagnosis: Coughing for more than 2 weeks, loss of weight, loss of appetite, fever and night sweats, fatigue are common symptoms of tuberculosis. TB Treatment x For new TB cases, the treatment in intensive phase (IP) consists of four drugs: Isoniazid (INH), Rifampicin, Pyrazinamide and Ethambutol. x For previously treated cases of TB, the intensive phase is of 12 weeks, where injection streptomycin is given for eight weeks along with four drugs. x Most people with TB are cured by a strictly followed 6-month drug regimen. PMF IAS – Learn Smart 146 Multidrug-resistant TB (MDR-TB) x CBNAAT (Cartridges Based Nucleic Acid Amplification Test) is used for early diagnosis of MDR-TB. x In MDR-TB, the bacteria that cause TB develop resistance to antimicrobial drugs used to cure the disease. x MDR-TB does not respond to at least isoniazid and rifampicin, the 2 most powerful anti-TB drugs. x Treatment options for MDR-TB are limited, and expensive. x In some cases, even more severe drug-resistant TB may develop. Extensively drug-resistant TB (XDR-TB) x XDR-TB is a form of multidrug-resistant TB with additional resistance to more anti-TB drugs. x People who are resistant to isoniazid and rifampin, plus any fluoroquinolone and at least one of three inject- able second-line drugs (amikacin, kanamycin, or capreomycin) are said to have XDR-TB. Causes of multidrug resistant-TB x Multidrug resistance is caused due to mismanagement of treatment and person-to-person transmission. x Mismanagement of TB treatment involves inappropriate or incorrect use of antimicrobial drugs or use of ineffective formulations of drugs and premature treatment interruption. Treatment for drug-resistant TB x The treatment success in MDR-TB patients is about 54%, while it is just 30% in the case of XDR-TB patients. x A combination of eight drugs for more than a year is need for XDR-TB treatment. x Treatment success in XDR-TB patients depends on the extent of the drug resistance, the severity of the dis- ease, whether the patient’s immune system is weakened, and adherence to treatment. x Drugs used for treating MDR-TB and XDR-TB can cause serious adverse effects such as deafness. The goal to end TB by 2025 x Revised National TB Control Programme was renamed as the National TB Elimination Programme (NTEP). x The change in name is in line with the larger goal of eliminating the disease by 2025, five years ahead of the Sustainable Development Goals target. x NTEP got a much needed boost with the WHO stating that TrueNat MTB has high diagnostic accuracy. x As a first step, TrueNat MTB will be available at community health centres and would slowly be extended to primary health centres across the country. x There are 5,500-6,000 community health centres and about 25,000 PHCs. PMF IAS – Learn Smart 147 x The states will be procuring the diagnostic machine directly from the Goa-based manufacturer. National TB Elimination Programme (NTEP) x 1962: The National TB Programme (NTP) was launched by GOI with BCG vaccination at the district level. x 1993: WHO declared TB as a global emergency and devised the directly observed treatment (DOTS). x 1993: GOI revitalized NTP as Revised National TB Control Programme (RNTCP). x 1997: DOTS was launched as the RNTCP strategy. By 2006 the entire country was covered under RNTCP. x In its second phase (2006–11), RNTCP improved the quality and reach of services. x Despite the measures, undiagnosed and mistreated cases continued to drive the TB epidemic. x A large number of MDR-TB cases were reported every year. x To address this, National Strategic Plan for Tuberculosis Control 2012-2017 was documented with the goal of ‘universal access to quality TB diagnosis and treatment’. x Significant interventions were taken during NSP 2012-2017 in terms of mandatory notification of all TB cases, integration of the programme with the National Health Mission, etc. x To eliminate TB in India by 2025, National Strategic Plan for Tuberculosis Elimination 2017-2025 in- volving all the stakeholders was formulated by RNTCP. x On 01-01-2020, RNTCP was renamed as National TB Elimination Programme (NTEP). National strategic plan for tuberculosis elimination (NSP) 2017-2025 (NSP) x TB elimination has been integrated into the four strategic pillars of “Detect – Treat – Prevent – Build” (DTPB). Detect x Early diagnosis and treatment of TB is an important step in TB elimination. x The objective of NSP was to find all drug sensitive TB cases (DS-TB) and drug resistant TB cases (DRTB). x To facilitate TB notification, RNTCP has developed a TB surveillance system called “NIKSHAY” (https://nik- shay.gov.in) for both government and private health care facilities. x For TB diagnosis more than 14,000 designated microscopy centres spread across the country. x Cartridge Based Nucleic Acid Amplification Tests (CBNAAT) / Line Probe Assay (LPA) have been estab- lished at district levels for decentralised molecular testing for drug resistant TB. x From 2020, GOI will be using Truenat test as a part of early stage diagnosis. Treat x Screening of all patients for rifampicin resistance (and for additional drugs wherever indicated) is done. PMF IAS – Learn Smart 148 x For drug sensitive TB, daily fixed dose combinations (FDCs) of first-line anti-tuberculosis drugs are given. x First line treatment of drug-sensitive TB consists of a 1. two-months intensive phase with four drug FDCs (Isoniazid (INH), Rifampicin, Pyrazinamide and Eth- ambutol (HRZE)) followed by a 2. continuation phase of four months with three drug FDCs (Rifampicin, Isoniazid, and Ethambutol (HRE)). x For previously treated cases of TB, the intensive Phase is of three months, where 1. injection streptomycin is given for two months along with four drugs (HRZE) and 2. then four drugs (HRZE) are continued for another month. 3. In continuation phase Rifampicin, INH, and Ethambutol are continued for another five months. Prevent x Isoniazid Preventive Therapy (IPT) is given to Children who are close contacts of a TB patient. x BCG vaccination is provided at birth or as early as possible till one year of age. x BCG vaccine has a protective effect against meningitis and disseminated TB in children. Build x Health system strengthening for TB control under the NSP 2017-2025 is recommended in the form of building and strengthening enabling policies, empowering institutions, and human resources. Typhoid fever x Typhoid fever is caused by the highly contagious Salmonella Typhi bacteria. x The bacteria spreads through contaminated food or water. x While typhoid bacteria can be treated with antibiotics, the microbes have developed resistance against mul- tiple antibiotics. x Multi-drug resistant typhoid bacteria are seen in south Asia including India. x Extensively drug-resistant (XDR) typhoid has been found in India, Bangladesh, and Pakistan. Miscellaneous Topics Criticality x Criticality is a nuclear term that refers to the balance of neutrons in the system. x Balance of neutrons can be achieved using moderators & control rods. PMF IAS – Learn Smart 149 x “Subcritical” refers to a system where the loss rate of neutrons is greater than the production rate of neu- trons & therefore the neutron population decreases as time goes on. x “Supercritical” refers to a system where the production rate of neutrons is greater than the loss rate of neutrons & therefore the neutron population increases. x When the neutron population remains constant, this means there is a perfect balance between production rate & loss rate, & the nuclear system is said to be “critical.” x When a reactor is starting up, the neutron population is increased slowly in a controlled manner, so that more neutrons are produced than are lost, & the nuclear reactor becomes supercritical. x When the desired power level is achieved, the nuclear reactor is placed into a critical configuration to keep the neutron population & power constant. x Finally, during shutdown, the reactor is placed in a subcritical configuration so that the neutron population & power decreases. x Therefore, when a reactor is said to have “gone critical,” it actually means it is in a stable configuration producing a constant power! 9 Supercritical == Car [nuclear reactor] is accelerating. 9 Critical == Car is going at a constant speed. 9 Sub critical == Car is slowing down. Graphene x Graphene is a two-dimensional single layer (monolayer) of carbon atoms linked in a hexagonal lattice. x It is an allotrope of carbon. x It is also known as “The Wonder Material”/miracle material x It is harder than diamond yet more elastic than rubber; tougher than steel yet lighter than aluminium. x Graphene is the thinnest compound known to man at one atom thick. x It is the lightest material known (with 1 square meter weighing around 0.77 milligrams). x It is the strongest compound discovered (between 100-300 times stronger than steel). x It is the best conductor of heat at room temperature, and also the best conductor of electricity known. x It is nearly transparent. x It is impermeable to gases. x Graphene is known for anti-bacterial properties. x Graphene has emerged as one of the most promising nanomaterials because of its unique combination of superb properties. PMF IAS – Learn Smart 150 Properties of Graphene Electronic properties x The atomic arrangement of the carbon atoms in graphene allows electrons to easily travel at extremely high velocity without the significant chance of scattering, saving precious energy typically. Mechanical properties x The impressive intrinsic mechanical properties are caused by the stability of the sp2 bonds that form the hexagonal lattice and oppose a variety of in-plane deformations. Uses of Graphene 1. Energy storage and solar cells 2. Lubrication 3. Graphene ink 4. Transistors and memory 5. Flexible, stretchable and foldable electronics 6. Photodetectors 7. Face Mask, etc. Malware (malicious software) x Malware is any program or file that is harmful to an electronic device user. x Malware can perform a variety of functions such as stealing, encrypting, deleting sensitive data, altering or hijacking core computing functions and monitoring users' computer activity without their permission. x Mobile malware can provide access to the device's components such as the camera, microphone, GPS, etc. x Malware can be delivered to a device with a USB drive or can spread over the internet through downloads without the user's approval or knowledge. PMF IAS – Learn Smart 151 x Phishing attacks are another common type of malware delivery where emails disguised as legitimate mes- sages contain malicious links or attachments that can deliver the malware executable to unsuspecting users. Different types of malware x Virus: malware which can execute itself and spread by infecting other programs or files. x Worm: self-replicating malware that typically spreads without any human interaction or directives. x Trojan horse: designed to appear as a legitimate program in order to gain access to a system. Once acti- vated, Trojans can execute their malicious functions. x Spyware: malware that collects data on the device and observe user activity without their knowledge. x Ransomware: malware that infects a user's system and encrypts the data. Cybercriminals then demand a ransom payment from the victim in exchange for decrypting the system's data. x The 2017 WannaCry ransomware attack targeted computers running the Microsoft Windows operating system by encrypting data and demanding ransom payments in the Bitcoin cryptocurrency. x Rootkit: malware created to obtain administrator-level access to the victim's system. Once installed, the program gives threat actors root or privileged access to the system. x Adware: malware used to track a user’s browser and download history with the intent to display pop-up or banner advertisements that lure the user into making a purchase. x Keyloggers: also called system monitors, are used to see nearly everything a user does on their computer. This includes emails, opened web-pages, programs and keystrokes. Super Apps x A super app is a platform developed by a company offering various services under one umbrella app. x For example, China’s WeChat, which started out as a messaging app, expanded into payments, cabs, shop- ping, food ordering, cab services to become a super app. Which companies in India are building super apps? x The Tata Group will be an entrant in an already crowded super app ecosystem of India. x Reliance Industries, under its Jio umbrella. x Alibaba Group investee Paytm. x Flipkart Group-owned payments app PhonePe. What are the concerns about Super Apps? x Increase in one company’s monopoly. PMF IAS – Learn Smart 152 x Concerns of privacy. x Data collected by the master app could then be used to train machines in artificial intelligence. Trans-Fat x As per WHO industrially produced trans-fats are found in hardened vegetable fats such as margarine and ghee (clarified butter) and are often present in snack foods, baked goods and fried foods. x The substance is responsible for around 500,000 deaths due to coronary heart disease every year across the world. x It is, however, often used by manufacturers because it has a longer shelf life and is cheaper than other, healthier choices that do not affect taste or cost. x So far, 58 countries introduced laws to protect 3.2 billion people from the substance by the end of 2021. x They did this by establishing mandatory limits for trans-fats to two per cent of oils and fats in all foods or by banning partially hydrogenated oils. x India has implemented less restrictive measures. Fats x Fat is one of the three main macronutrients: fat, carbohydrate, and protein. x Fat is a major source of energy and helps your body absorb vitamins. 9 Carbohydrates | Monosaccharides | Polysaccharides 9 Proteins | Amino Acids | Enzymes 9 Vitamins and Minerals – Deficiency Diseases x Fat has the most calories compared to any other nutrient. Controlling fat intake is one of the most im- portant steps in losing or maintaining weight and preventing or delaying type 2 diabetes. x Fats, also known as triglycerides, are esters of three fatty acid chains and the alcohol glycerol. x Fats are solids at room temperature. Oil refers to a fat with unsaturated fatty acid chains that is liquid at room temperature. x Fats, like other lipids, are generally insoluble in water. Saturated fat x A saturated fat is a fat in which the fatty acids all have single bonds. PMF IAS – Learn Smart 153 x A saturated fat has the maximum number of hydrogens bonded to the carbons, and therefore is ‘saturated’ with hydrogen atoms. x Most animal fats are saturated whereas the fats of plants and fish are generally unsaturated. x Many experts recommend a diet low in saturated fat. x Saturated fats are popular with manufacturers of processed foods because they are less vulnerable to ran- cidity and are, in general, more solid at room temperature than unsaturated fats. Unsaturated fat x An unsaturated fat is a fat or fatty acid in which there is at least one double bond within the fatty acid chain. x Where double bonds are formed, hydrogen atoms are eliminated. x In cellular metabolism, unsaturated fat molecules contain somewhat less energy (i.e., fewer calories) than an equivalent amount of saturated fat. x The greater the degree of unsaturation in a fatty acid (i.e., the more double bonds in the fatty acid) the more vulnerable it is to rancidity [lipid oxidation] [rusting of fats]. x Antioxidants can protect unsaturated fat from lipid oxidation. Unhealthy Fats – Saturated Fat and Trans Fat x The main types of “unhealthy” fats are saturated and trans-fat. x Saturated fats are primarily found in foods that come from animals, such as meat and dairy. x Saturated fats are unhealthy because they increase LDL (“bad” cholesterol) levels in your body. PMF IAS – Learn Smart 154 x Many saturated fats are “solid” fats that you can see, such as the fat in meat. x Other sources of saturated fats include high-fat cheese, butter, Ice cream, palm and coconut oils, etc. x Trans fats or trans-unsaturated fatty acids are a type of unsaturated fats that are uncommon in nature. x Trans fats are worse than saturated fats. x Trans fat is simply liquid oils turned into solid fats during food processing. x Natural trans-fats, present in very small amounts in certain animal products, are not considered harmful. x But industrially-produced artificial trans-fats (manufactured by adding hydrogen to vegetable oil) lead to an increase in bad cholesterol (LDL) and lowering of good cholesterol (HDL). x Foods containing trans-fat are usually labelled as “partially hydrogenated”. x Partially hydrogenated oil is less likely to spoil, so foods made with it have a longer shelf life. x Trans fats are easy to use, inexpensive to produce and last a long time. x Trans fats give foods a desirable taste and texture. x These trans-fats are largely found in vanaspati oil, margarine, bakery shortenings, and in baked and fried foods.
